messages:
maria g: Quick follow-up to the RFC — for Private mode are we leaning per-customer VPC peering or a shared control-plane with private endpoints? Need a short list of tradeoffs for the onboarding doc.

sam w: If customers need full network isolation, peering wins. But peering means more VPCs, more route tables, and operational overhead on setup. :thinking:

jon r: Shared control-plane + private endpoints reduces AWS account noise and makes rollouts simpler. Downside is cross-account connectivity and KMS access patterns we need to design for.

priya s: Also logging/audit implications: with peering egress stays in-customer and they control retention. With shared control plane we have to push/replicate logs into customer S3 or expose export connectors. Slight privacy/regulatory friction.

kevin: SLA/latency note — peering often gives lower p99 for control-plane RPCs. Endpoints add a hop (VPC endpoint NAT/proxy) but if colocated in-region it should be small. Need perf numbers.

alice: Suggestion: default to shared endpoints for self-serve onboarding; offer peering as a premium/enterprise option for regulated customers. Keeps initial ops simple. :thumbsup:

sam w: Agree. Also define clear interface boundaries: control-plane RPCs must be idempotent and retry-safe if endpoints fail. Auth should support both cross-account IAM roles and mTLS for agent scenarios.

maria g: What about the agent/sidecar relay we discussed? Good for on-prem/air-gapped, but it adds customer-side ops and versioning headaches.

jon r: Agent/relay is the right long-term escape hatch for air-gapped. For cloud VPCs a lightweight relay that tunnels control-plane protobufs/TLS could standardize across both models. We should spec the protocol surface (register, heartbeat, RPC proxy).

priya s: I'll add a short terraform snippet for the onboarding docs so infra teams can copy/paste. Example: ```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_cp" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx"
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids   = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [var.sg_control_plane]
}
```

infra-bot: Deploy-check: control-plane endpoints prototype deployed to staging in us-west-2 (run id: deploy-2026-03-20-01) :white_check_mark:

kevin: Action items: 1) short doc with tradeoffs + recommended default; 2) migration path for customers wanting to switch to peering; 3) auth patterns (cross-account IAM + mTLS) + template roles; 4) perf test plan (p99 control-plane latency). I'll own perf tests.

maria g: I'll draft the tradeoffs doc and migration outline. @pri ya? (cc @pri ya s) — want first draft by EOW so we can sync with Eng infra.

priya s: I'll add the terraform examples and logging/export options. EOW works for me.

alice: I'll put together a quick cost model (peering vs endpoints vs agent) and a slide for the exec sync.

maria g: Thanks — we'll consolidate into a single follow-up RFC with migration steps.

sam w: One more: we should include a fallback policy — if control-plane endpoints are unreachable, auto-failover to public API with customer-approved routing (opt-in). That reduces outage blast radius.

jon r: +1 on fallback. Also add a checklist for customers to validate: route table, SGs, KMS grants, IAM trust.

maria g: Perfect. Will open a PR with the doc tomorrow and tag @architecture for review.
